node_count.note: 139,255 expert-proofread neurons in the whole-brain FlyWire connectome; 127,978 form the high-confidence graph at >=5 synapse threshold (graph used for all stats below).

density.note: Overall directed connection probability. Derived from rich-club internal probability 0.000870 / 5.4x; independent adjacency check (2,613,129 edges / 127,978^2) gives 0.0001595 (~0.016%).

weighted_synapses.note: 15.1M directed weighted edges in the stats graph; ~54.5M raw chemical synapses in the full connectome; ~32M survive the >=5 threshold.

rich_club_pct.unit: % of connectome (40,218 neurons, cut-off total degree k>37)
rich_club_pct.note: Rich-club regime vs degree-preserving (CFG) null: cut-off total degree 37, containing 40,218 neurons (~30%). Against 127,978 graph = 31.4%; vs full 139,255 = 28.9%; Lin et al. report ~30%.

rich_club_density_mult.note: Rich-club internal connection probability 0.000870 = 5.4x the overall 0.000161.

reciprocity.note: 77,607 of 127,978 neurons (~2 in 3) participate in >=1 reciprocal connection; avg 23% incoming / 18% outgoing connections reciprocal. Reciprocity higher than ER and CFG nulls.

small_world_S.note: Driven by clustering C^Delta 0.0463 vs ER null 0.0003 (~154x) with little avg-path penalty (undirected 3.91 vs ER 3.57). C. elegans = 3.21; internet = 98.1.

avg_directed_path.note: Avg shortest directed path in giant SCC = 4.42 hops, every neuron reachable within 13; undirected (WCC) avg 3.91, max 11.

scc_pct.unit: % of neurons in single strongly-connected component
scc_pct.note: 93.3% of neurons in one SCC, 98.8% in one WCC. Robust to pruning strongest/weakest edges and synapse threshold.

robustness_note.value: Distributed fault tolerance; survives ~60% neuron removal; NO dominant command-hub neurons (unlike C. elegans AVA/AVB). Removing neurons by largest total degree, first SCC persists until total degree 50 (then splits into left/right hemispheres surviving ~60% removal); removing smallest-degree neurons never divides the SCC.

null_model.finding: CONTESTED. Exact connectome wiring does NOT reliably beat a well-constructed degree-preserving null on EARLY-LEARNING-EFFICIENCY metrics (Dhiman 2026: advantage vanishes under fair shared init + degree-preserving rewiring, loss diff -0.0020 vanished to +0.0003), but DOES beat it on FINAL-TASK CONTROL PERFORMANCE (FlyGM: 8.29 vs 13.55 deg angle error) and on input-routing / dominant-mode identity (Therianos; Creamer/Leifer/Pillow C. elegans activity prediction). GATE RULE: generators MUST NOT over-claim a connectome 'learning advantage'. Degree-preserving nulls + shared-initialization controls are the mandatory baseline; naive sparse-random controls are not acceptable. Any learning-advantage claim must cite which regime (early-learning vs convergence) and must be weight-matched where applicable (both headline nulls have caveats: Dhiman's is not cell-type/motif-aware; FlyGM's is unweighted).
